title: Steel Exchange India Ltd - 534748 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 19.45% QoQ to INR 287.70 crore and EBITDA margin to 17.41%, with net profit at INR 12.37 crore.
summary.overview: Total income for Q4 FY26 was INR 287.70 crore, up 19.45% QoQ from INR 240.86 crore. EBITDA rose 118.12% QoQ to INR 50.10 crore, with margin up 788 bps to 17.41%. Net profit was INR 12.37 crore versus INR 2.28 crore in Q3, with a 4.30% net margin. For FY26, total income was INR 1,066.42 crore, EBITDA INR 138.03 crore and net profit INR 26.99 crore. Management said it redeemed INR 43.19 crore of NCDs in one tranche and cut debt by nearly INR 68 crore over the last two quarters.

segments.name: TMT rebar / long products (Simhadri brand)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 rebar volume was 49,760 tonnes, up from about 39,000 t in Q3. Management said the average EBITDA per tonne was about INR 9,000-9,500 in the last quarter versus about INR 6,000 in earlier quarters, and about INR 6,800-7,000 on a yearly average.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: Power segment revenue fell in FY26. Management attributed this to kiln refurbishments; it expects data-centre tie-ups and capacity expansion to improve consumption.

segments.name: Logistics (SEIL Logistics and Infra Company)
segments.commentary: A subsidiary formed to run a private freight terminal and logistics at Visakhapatnam, with railway sidings. MoUs with the Andhra Pradesh government cover about 150 acres adjacent to the existing land.

guidance_outlook: Management said Q4 FY26 is 'fine' but later years should be better; it expects steady margins while the market stays buoyant.
Management expects FY27 volumes to roughly double once the reheating furnace and capacity expansion come on stream from Q2 FY27, with capacity mostly doubled.
Sustainable EBITDA guidance given as about INR 7,000 per tonne on average volumes of 40,000-50,000 tonnes per quarter.

Finance cost is expected at about INR 12-13 crore per quarter, not below 10, after the new loan costs and trade finance charges fall away. Refinancing is targeted to bring the cost of debt to about 9%.

Existing capex (reheating furnace, furnace refurbishment, kiln work) is to be completed in FY27. New greenfield capex for the 1 million tonne green steel plant is about one year away, pending groundbreaking and the strategic investor's inputs.
Pledged shares are expected to be released once refinancing is complete and IMR funds are received.
capex_capacity: A reheating furnace is being installed, expected to start from Q2 FY27 and to add about 50,000 tonnes of new bar capacity. Management said it will raise rolling mill efficiency by 30-40%.
Billet and rebar capacities were raised by about 44-45% at the end of FY25. Utilisation is about 46-47% for rebar and 55-56% for billet, with a target of 70-75% in FY27.
Expansions already under way are expected to be operational by end-July 2026.
Land bank: about 400-450 acres existing; another 150 acres targeted for the logistics park and 150 acres for steel manufacturing. MoUs cover a 1 million tonne green steel plant.
Planned capex and debt paydown are to be funded from INR 300 crore of share warrant money from IMR Group and internal accruals.
demand_pricing: Management said the Indian steel outlook is strong, citing infrastructure, housing, railways, defence and import substitution. It also said Andhra Pradesh and Visakhapatnam projects (Google AI hub, ArcelorMittal, Amaravati) are sources of demand, and that the company is an approved vendor for them.
April 2026 sales were described as 'great' and May as slightly weaker due to heatwave and the war situation. Management expects a June recovery.
Management said the company is largely insulated from the ongoing war, except for some diesel cost in transport. Coal, iron ore and scrap are sourced locally.
The company was re-empanelled under MES for TMT bar supplies to the Ministry of Defence.

qa_highlights.question: What does the company plan to fund its capacity growth and reduce its debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has MoUs with state governments for expansion and a 1 million tonne green steel plant. Project reports are pending, and the plan is to announce them once formalised.

qa_highlights.question: When is the balance payment expected from IMR on the share warrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR 300 crore warrant subscription is expected within about six months and will fund growth, including green steel.

qa_highlights.question: What is the finance cost trend, and why did it rise QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 finance cost was INR 7.50 crore, not INR 17 crore. The analyst then cited Q3 at INR 13 crore and Q4 at INR 17 crore; management attributed the difference to new loan processing costs and supplier trade finance. Term debt has fallen from about INR 350 crore to INR 250 crore, and current debt is about INR 270 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What were rebar volumes and what is the FY27 volume outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 FY26 rebar sales were 49,760 tonnes. Management said FY27 capacity is expected to roughly double from Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current capacity utilisation and when will it reach 85-90%?
qa_highlights.answer: Rebar utilisation is about 46-47% and billet about 55-56%. Management expects 70-75% in FY27 after the reheating furnace is commissioned.

qa_highlights.question: Why are the company's shares 100% pledged, and will this change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the pledge is linked to past bank exposure. It expects the pledge to be released after refinancing, to a debt cost of about 9%, and once IMR funds are received.

risks_watch: Debt and funding: the IMR INR 300 crore warrant money has not yet been received and is expected in about six months. Refinancing to about 9% is planned but not yet closed.
Finance cost: management guided to INR 12-13 crore per quarter, which is well above the analyst's expected single-digit level.
Margin sustainability: the EBITDA margin of 17.41% is above the earlier 11-12% range, and management called the steel market 'buoyant' but cyclical.
Execution: FY27 volume doubling depends on the reheating furnace and expansions running from Q2 FY27.
Demand softness in May 2026 due to heatwave and war-related conditions.
Governance: management agreed to consider quarterly investor calls, which are not yet in place.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the turnaround and FY27 growth. Management was less precise on the finance cost, the capex size and the timing of the warrant funds, and it gave several figures in a loose, non-standard form.
